## Wave 12 systemic integration packet — Shelter Automation And Power

The principal owner set is **power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners**. The material anchors are **a warm switch, a quiet pipe, an old notice, and a cue understood with sound off**. The observable marker set is **load priority, reserve warmth, maintenance pause, outage age, and restart confidence**. This packet is evidence scaffolding, not an implementation claim. It keeps the eleventh-wave 30-field structure intact while adding a new review boundary for the twelfth wave.

### Integration packet 1 — Premise and collision receipt

Begin with a current-source search for every proposed fact, identifier, command, event, save section, and consumer. Record the exact owner among **power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners**, the read route, the mutation route, the event boundary, and the reason the existing seam can carry the behavior. Search synonyms, retired plan names, JSON catalogs, host panels, and tests before reserving a name. If the seam is absent, duplicated, or already claimed, keep the material as a bounded proposal, write the stop line, and do not invent a parallel authority. The receipt must state whether each field is authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable mutable state.

### Integration packet 2 — Command, observer, and interruption route

Trace one complete player loop from entry signal through validation, cost, event publication, provider refresh, and visible feedback. Define accepted, rejected, deferred, interrupted, repeated, and stale commands with human-readable reasons. The panel or route exposes **load priority, reserve warmth, maintenance pause, outage age, and restart confidence** as facts, never as a local counter. Include empty, loading, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states, plus the safe action available from each state. Close, back, host reload, controller disconnect, and focus restoration return to a truthful state without double-spending or silently discarding a reservation.

### Integration packet 3 — State, save, migration, and replay contract

Separate durable facts from projections and transient request state. Name the current codec and save-section owner, schema version, old-save default, null semantics, malformed-input response, checksum impact, and migration diagnostics. Exercise offer, acceptance, active work, pause, completion, failure, expiry, correction, and replay while saving at each boundary. Repeat the same seed and ordered inputs before and after reload, host reopen, duplicate event delivery, and interrupted command. Deterministic ordering must not depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, or hash iteration. Restore rebuilds projections from canonical state and never stores a second mutable copy.

### Integration packet 4 — Host, accessibility, and performance envelope

Specify the provider, route, panel, focus order, command map, and refresh source before describing UI polish. Test keyboard-only, controller-only, pointer, text scaling, long localization, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off cues, and invalid input. Set a bounded record count, pagination strategy, refresh cadence, event fan-out, allocation budget, save delta, and safe degradation rule. State cache ownership and invalidation explicitly. A large catalog must remain useful when optional rows, icons, audio, or remote-like references are missing; loading and error states must never block the player from backing out.

### Integration packet 5 — Story, side quest, callback, and rollback receipt

Tie each proposed mechanic to one person, place, object, or routine with a material detail: **a warm switch, a quiet pipe, an old notice, and a cue understood with sound off**. Define a practical disturbance, at least two interpretations, a meaningful cost, a refusal route, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcome, and a delayed callback in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Record publisher, consumer, consequence owner, duplicate-command policy, reservation release, and rollback. If a callback survives refusal, say why; if it retires, record the retirement condition. End with exact paths, focused verification, evidence gaps, collision risks, and the next premise audit.


## Wave 12 quality, prose, and branch packet — Shelter Automation And Power

The writing layer remains subordinate to the playable owner seam. Prose supplies evidence, motives, callbacks, and branch clarity; it does not create a second state machine.

### Quality packet 1 — Voice, evidence, and material detail

Write from what a person can see, carry, remember, repair, or verify. Give drivers, survivors, operators, cartographers, archivists, children, and witnesses different limits and vocabulary shaped by the same ashfall conditions. Use **a warm switch, a quiet pipe, an old notice, and a cue understood with sound off** as recurring evidence rather than exposition. Dialogue stays short enough for localization and readable UI; a pause, correction, or unfinished sentence can carry uncertainty. Every content row receives a source note, localization key, correction path, and owner reference. Avoid generic quest verbs, omniscient summaries, and rewards that exist only to justify a branch.

### Quality packet 2 — Side-quest branch and consequence table

For every seed, document entry fact, first interpretation, competing interpretation, player choice, resource or time cost, refusal, quiet success, costly success, unresolved result, callback, repeat policy, and retirement. At least one branch changes a reachable state or provider projection owned by an existing system. A prose-only branch is insufficient. A refused request must leave a coherent world state, and a delayed callback must explain what the player can now observe. Include a versioned content key and migration note so a content correction does not erase a player’s evidence.

### Quality packet 3 — High-volume authoring and pagination discipline

Start with a canonical sample and expand through the current loader and validator. Each row carries a stable snake_case ID, schema version, source reference, lifecycle state, localization key, failure reason, owner, and rollback note. Reject duplicate identifiers, unsupported effects, unresolved references, contradictory status values, duplicate prose, and rows with no consumer. Define pagination, grouping, search, filtering, and stale-row handling. Measure refresh, allocations, event fan-out, save delta, and truncation behavior against the stated budget; preserve a useful first page if the full bank is unavailable.

### Quality packet 4 — Failure, recovery, and callback theatre

Choose one understandable failure such as fog, fatigue, grief, outage, disputed provenance, stale notice, or missing witness. Show the player the cause, the evidence that remains, the safe recovery, and the delayed effect of choosing to wait. Retry through the same owner command with deterministic ordering. Do not hide a penalty in a panel cache or make recovery depend on a new currency. The receipt names the callback surface, the observer fact, the reservation release, the rollback condition, and the stop line when a premise cannot be demonstrated.


## Wave 12 cross-system consequence matrix — Shelter Automation And Power

Each consequence below names a source, consumer, visible result, and recovery route. The matrix is a design review aid and must be checked against current source before implementation.

### Consequence field 1 — Input fact map

List canonical starting facts, publisher, freshness, source reference, empty semantics, and intentionally unavailable data. Consumers use stable IDs or provider results and never reconstruct mutable state from copied fields. For **load priority, reserve warmth, maintenance pause, outage age, and restart confidence**, write the normal, stale, missing, and contradictory cases and state which owner wins. A projection can summarize several owners only if its inputs and refresh boundary are explicit.

### Consequence field 2 — Player-facing consequence

Describe the visible route, command, cost, uncertainty, and result. The outcome changes an existing state or projection that a player can inspect later, such as route confidence, contact boundary, reserve warmth, or coordinate provenance. Do not invent a new currency, ledger, graph, grid, map, archive, or privacy store. The player must be able to tell what changed and what remains unknown.

### Consequence field 3 — Delayed callback

Name a later journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition callback using a stable result from the current owner. Explain how the callback behaves after refusal, deferral, reload, correction, and retirement. Give it a physical clue and a readable source label so the player can connect the earlier decision without a lore dump.

### Consequence field 4 — Refusal, recovery, and permissions

Show pause, refusal, and recovery without a hidden punishment. Failed commands explain cause, release reservations, preserve evidence, and retry through the same owner. Permission or consent boundaries do not silently extend when a task is delegated. If another character accepts the work, record the handoff and the new observer fact; if nobody accepts, keep the unresolved state visible.

### Consequence field 5 — Stale, duplicate, and interruption fixture

Exercise stale save, missing reference, duplicate event, repeated command, host close, provider refresh during input, and interruption during a costly action. Expect one authoritative state, one visible update where appropriate, deterministic event order, checksum evidence, and safe rollback. A duplicate should be idempotent or explicitly rejected; it must never grant the same reward or consume the same item twice.

### Consequence field 6 — Handoff and review boundary

Name exact paths, IDs, data classification, save decision, focused checks, UI accessibility evidence, performance budget, rollback, collision risk, unowned mechanics, and next premise audit. Classify the packet as data-only, data-plus-wiring, Core extension, or cross-system. The matrix is complete only when a reviewer can reproduce the claim from current source and identify what remains intentionally untouched.

## Continuation Wave 12 acceptance matrix — Shelter Automation And Power

This matrix gates the eleven new passes, high-volume bank, narrative and side-quest dossier, systemic integration packet, quality and branch packet, consequence matrix, and active 30-field plan layer. Every row requires current-source evidence before an implementation status can change.

### 01 — Premise receipt

For this plan, **premise receipt** requires that Recheck the current owner, public API, catalog, runtime consumer, save section, and worktree claim in source. A plan sentence, old test name, or stale audit cannot prove that the seam still exists. If a source path, event, or consumer is absent, retain the proposal with a written stop line and do not create a parallel route. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 02 — Single authority

For this plan, **single authority** requires that Name one mutable-state owner, one event seam for each fact, one authored-data authority, and one save-section owner where persistence is required. Panels, descriptors, caches, and story packets may summarize facts but may not keep counters, ledgers, relationship graphs, grids, maps, archives, or privacy stores of their own. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 03 — Data and migration

For this plan, **data and migration** requires that Validate stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, defaults, and record-level diagnostics. Define behavior for a missing row, unknown field, malformed catalog, duplicate ID, old save, and corrected copy. JSON presence is not reachability; a consumer, route, and observable result must be named. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 04 — State transitions

For this plan, **state transitions** requires that Prove offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states across interruption, reload, stale save, invalid input, and duplicate delivery. Record who may issue each command, what resource is reserved, how it is released, and which event fact is visible to observers. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 05 — Player and host route

For this plan, **player and host route** requires that Trace input to owner validation and back to feedback. Empty, loading, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states must explain cause and safe next action. Back and close return focus to the invoking control; a host reload restores the same truthful projection without replaying a reward or losing a refusal. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 06 — Cross-system consequence

For this plan, **cross-system consequence** requires that Identify at least three existing domains and record publisher, consumer, consequence owner, freshness, and delayed callback. Subscribers read facts and request commands through the owner; they do not mutate another subsystem from a callback. Contradictory facts specify precedence or remain visibly uncertain. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 07 — Story and side quest

For this plan, **story and side quest** requires that Include a practical disturbance, distinct voice, material clue, meaningful resource or time cost, competing interpretation, refusal, quiet success, costly success, unresolved result, and delayed callback. The side quest must alter a reachable state or projection and must keep a coherent world after the player declines. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 08 — Narrative branch proof

For this plan, **narrative branch proof** requires that Verify that each branch changes a command result, durable fact, provider projection, relationship boundary, route condition, or archive status. Define repeat policy, retirement condition, and callback behavior after reload and content correction. A different paragraph without a systemic consequence is not a branch proof. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 09 — High-volume authoring

For this plan, **high-volume authoring** requires that Start with a valid canonical sample, then expand through the current loader and validator. Reject duplicate IDs, unsupported effects, unresolved references, contradictory lifecycle states, generic fetch loops, and rows with no consumer. State pagination, grouping, search, localization expansion, and safe truncation for the full bank. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 10 — Threshold field layer

For this plan, **threshold field layer** requires that Confirm that all thirty active fields remain distinct: the original fields, the post-threshold fields, and the current Wave 12 fields. For each, name its owner evidence, data classification, player route, replay case, accessibility check, performance budget, and rollback. Do not treat word count as completion or convert a field into a duplicate glossary. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 11 — Accessibility

For this plan, **accessibility** requires that Verify keyboard, controller, pointer, focus restoration, text scale, localization expansion, contrast, reduced motion, non-color cues, sound-off alternatives, and invalid-input recovery. Long names and uncertainty must remain readable. A player can cancel, defer, and recover from every proposed route without relying on a single sensory channel. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 12 — Performance

For this plan, **performance** requires that Exercise pagination, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, long strings, event fan-out, allocations, save size, and safe degradation. State an explicit budget and the owner of caching and invalidation. A high-volume bank may be paged or summarized, but its first page must remain truthful and interactive under the target load. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 13 — Persistence

For this plan, **persistence** requires that Round-trip only durable facts through the current codec and owner. Rebuild projections after restore, define migration defaults and malformed-save refusal, and preserve checksum, null, ordering, and deletion semantics. A save during a costly action must either resume deterministically or show a documented safe interruption state. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 14 — Determinism

For this plan, **determinism** requires that The same seed and ordered inputs before and after a save boundary, reload, repeated event, interruption, and host reopen must produce the same result and state hash. No wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUID, unordered dictionary, or incidental callback order may choose a gameplay outcome. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 15 — Rollback

For this plan, **rollback** requires that Failed commands are idempotent or explicitly rejected, reservations release safely, permissions do not silently extend, and evidence survives. Rollback restores prior owner state without deleting unrelated records. A migration or content correction has a reversible path and a diagnostic that tells the integrator what was skipped. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 16 — Handoff evidence

For this plan, **handoff evidence** requires that List exact files, IDs, owner claims, commands, focused verification, observed results, limitations, collision risks, unowned mechanics, and any Godot runtime evidence required. Keep production code and data untouched until a named implementation package claims the paths and the premise audit passes. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 17 — Closeout boundary

For this plan, **closeout boundary** requires that The document remains a DRAFT expansion scaffold. It does not claim that a catalog row is loaded, a panel is wired, a save section exists, or a side quest is reachable. Any implementation status belongs in the live integration ledger and requires current-source evidence, focused checks, and an explicit handoff. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

### 18 — Wave completion receipt

For this plan, **wave completion receipt** requires that Record the twelve-wave cumulative count, the new pass range 111–121, ten high-volume fields, twelve story packets, systemic, quality, consequence, and acceptance sections, measured word total, and intentionally untouched paths. State known gaps and the next premise audit. Planning volume is a capacity signal, never runtime proof. The receipt records the owner path, command or read route, observable result, limitation, and rollback evidence.

This pass tests how **demand signal calibration** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Demand Signal Calibration receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Shelter Resilience Assembly receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Shelter Resilience Assembly receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 15 compact integration and acceptance packet — Shelter Automation And Power

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **shelter thresholds and recovery**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 16 — Plan 7 — Shelter Automation And Power

Wave 16 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **shelter automation and power**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a load tag in chalk, a valve wrapped in cloth, a lamp carried to the night shift, and a notice signed aloud**. Observable markers include **load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness**.

### Pass 155 — Demand Threshold Cards

This pass tests how **demand threshold cards** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners; it does not add a second shelter automation and power authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with the material anchors a load tag in chalk, a valve wrapped in cloth, a lamp carried to the night shift, and a notice signed aloud. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Demand Threshold Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

### Pass 166 — Demand Threshold Review

This pass tests how **demand threshold review** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners; it does not add a second shelter automation and power authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with the material anchors a load tag in chalk, a valve wrapped in cloth, a lamp carried to the night shift, and a notice read back aloud. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. **Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Demand Threshold Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 18 compact integration and acceptance packet — Shelter Automation And Power

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **shelter witness and commons**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

### Pass 188 — Demand Threshold Appeals

This pass tests how **demand threshold appeals** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners; it does not add a second shelter automation and power authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with the material anchors a breaker tally under glass, a valve wrapped in cloth, a lamp moved to the night shift, and a notice initialed aloud. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. **Demand Threshold Appeals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners; it does not add a second shelter automation and power authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with the material anchors a breaker tally under glass, a valve wrapped in cloth, a lamp moved to the night shift, and a notice initialed aloud. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Filter Change Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

### Pass 199 — Demand Threshold Charter

This pass tests how **demand threshold charter** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners; it does not add a second shelter automation and power authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Demand Threshold Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Demand Threshold Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Demand Threshold Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Demand Threshold Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Demand Threshold Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 20 compact integration and acceptance packet — Shelter Automation And Power

## Continuation Wave 21 — Plan 7 — Shelter Automation And Power

Wave 21 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **shelter automation and power**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a breaker tally on a clipboard, a valve wrapped in cloth, a lamp held by the night crew, and a notice read twice aloud**. Observable markers include **load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness**.

### Pass 210 — Demand Threshold Records

This pass tests how **demand threshold records** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners; it does not add a second shelter automation and power authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Demand Threshold Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Demand Threshold Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Demand Threshold Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Demand Threshold Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Demand Threshold Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. #### Field 3 — Data Contract

**Shelter Commons Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

**Shelter Commons Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

**Shelter Commons Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 22 compact integration and acceptance packet — Shelter Automation And Power

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **shelter record and signal**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 23 — Plan 7 — Shelter Automation And Power

Wave 23 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **shelter automation and power**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a breaker tally on a clipboard, a valve held by the night crew, a lamp held at the night shift, and a notice read twice aloud**. Observable markers include **load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness**.

### Pass 232 — Demand Threshold Signals

This pass tests how **demand threshold signals** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over power, water, air, building, schedule, duty, needs, and accessibility owners; it does not add a second shelter automation and power authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross load priority, reserve warmth, outage age, maintenance reason, pressure confidence, and restart readiness with the material anchors a breaker tally on a clipboard, a valve held by the night crew, a lamp held at the night shift, and a notice read twice aloud. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Demand Threshold Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 23 narrative and side-quest dossier — Shelter Automation And Power

These twelve packets turn the new **shelter proof and record** mechanics into grounded, replayable choices. They remain content-only until the canonical owner, consumer, save route, and deterministic result are proven. Each packet uses **a breaker tally on a clipboard, a valve held by the night crew, a lamp held at the night shift, and a notice read twice aloud** as physical evidence and preserves refusal, costly success, unresolved outcomes, and delayed callbacks.

A practical disturbance makes **the clipboard record** matter. The player can verify, accept, defer, share, or refuse. A person or place bears a material clue from **a breaker tally on a clipboard, a valve held by the night crew, a lamp held at the night shift, and a notice read twice aloud**; the clue returns later in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Quiet success protects a routine, costly success spends a real resource, and unresolved play leaves an honest unknown.
